description: Original Philippine herpetology descriptions, recent tarsier tracking and published Visayan Hornbill population sampling.

items.label: Adult body length
items.statement: The original type series measured 14.1–15.7 mm SVL in 10 adult males and 15.0 mm in one adult female.
items.source: Alcala, Brown & Diesmos (1998), Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 50:381–388
items.journal: Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences
items.scopeLimit: Original 1998 specimens; not a modern island-wide size distribution

items.label: Skin and toe disks
items.statement: The original diagnosis describes a smooth dorsum and toe disks broader than the finger disks.
items.source: Alcala, Brown & Diesmos (1998), Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 50:381–388
items.journal: Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences
items.scopeLimit: A combination of size, disks and call distinguishes small Platymantis

items.label: Male advertisement call
items.statement: The described call is a brief repeated 'tet-tet' chirp.
items.source: Alcala, Brown & Diesmos (1998), Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 50:381–388
items.journal: Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences
items.scopeLimit: 1998 recorded population, Northern Sierra Madre, Luzon

items.label: Adult body length
items.statement: Original samples measured 20.3–23.9 mm SVL in 18 adult males and 21.6–28.0 mm in 14 adult females.
items.source: Alcala, Brown & Diesmos (1998), Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 50:381–388
items.journal: Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences

items.label: Dorsal skin
items.statement: Head, eyelids and dorsum bear numerous tubercles and short, low, irregular dorsal ridges.
items.source: Alcala, Brown & Diesmos (1998), Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 50:381–388
items.journal: Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences
items.scopeLimit: Skin features vary within the original sample

items.label: Male advertisement call
items.statement: The described advertisement call is a repeated 'psik' note.
items.source: Alcala, Brown & Diesmos (1998), Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 50:381–388
items.journal: Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences

items.label: Banahao montane forest
items.statement: Original collections were from forest-floor habitat at 900–2,150 m on Mt. Banahao.
items.source: Alcala, Brown & Diesmos (1998), Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 50:381–388
items.journal: Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences
items.scopeLimit: Original locality observations, not an island-wide habitat model

items.label: Black-and-gold dorsal pattern
items.statement: The original diagnosis describes contrasting black and golden-yellow dorsal coloration.
items.scopeLimit: Diagnostic evidence includes several additional scale and reproductive characters

items.label: Juvenile throat
items.statement: The 2010 diagnosis records dark gular coloration in juveniles.
items.scopeLimit: Juvenile trait in the original description

items.label: Northern Sierra Madre
items.statement: The original study documents forests of the central and northern Sierra Madre, Luzon.
items.scopeLimit: The paper maps studied populations and distinguishes V. olivaceus to the south

items.label: Mangrove reserve sleeping sites
items.statement: Six radio-tracked tarsiers used 44 sleeping sites in Del Carmen Mangrove Reserve, Siargao.
items.source: Bejar et al. (2026), Folia Primatologica, online 25 March

items.label: Recorded roost plants
items.statement: Sleeping sites included screw pines, thickets, non-mangrove trees, Rhizophora and Nypa palms.
items.source: Bejar et al. (2026), Folia Primatologica, online 25 March
items.scopeLimit: Observed substrates in the studied mangrove reserve

items.label: Male home range
items.statement: Three tagged adult males had a mean minimum-convex-polygon home range of 3.16 ha.
items.source: Bejar et al. (2026), Folia Primatologica, online 25 March
items.scopeLimit: Three adult males; site and method specific

items.label: Forest density comparison
items.statement: Northwest Panay density estimates were 17.8 birds/km² in primary forest and 3.7 birds/km² in secondary forest.
items.scopeLimit: 2021 survey; coefficients of variation 26.9% and 33.2% respectively

items.label: Northwest Panay population estimate
items.statement: The 2021 distance-sampling study estimated 2,673 Visayan Hornbills across the Northwest Panay Peninsula.
items.scopeLimit: Estimate for a defined peninsula, not a national count; 95% CI 1,767–4,045

items.label: No detections in open sites
items.statement: Point counts found Visayan Hornbills in forest but not in surveyed plantations or open habitat.
items.scopeLimit: No detections in sampled plots does not establish species-wide absence
